name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 4, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor MacLean at
5:01 p.m., on January 4, 2010 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on December 23, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor MacLean

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Staff Absent:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ledesma

INVOCATION: Mayor MacLean

CLOSED SESSION

City Council Minutes  1  January 4, 2010
 CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel-Anticipated Litigation. Initiation of litigation
  pursuant to subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9: One case: Appeal of State
  Department of Water Resources Control Boards adoption of the NPDES permit.

CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Property: Turf Lane Open Space;
  25361 Turf Avenue (APN: 619-331-35) within the City of Mission Viejo; City
  Negotiator: City Manager Wilberg and City Attorney Curley; Negotiating Party:
  Timberline Community Homeowners Association and legal counsel. Under
  negotiation: Terms of Paymentconsideration and quitclaim deed from City to
  Timberline Community Homeowners Association.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor MacLean recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m., with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session item CS1, the City Council
approved the Appeal of the State Department of Water Resources Control Boards adoption of the
NPDES permit, followed by possible acceptance of a tolling agreement. The authorization to
proceed was approved with vote of 5-0.

For CS2, the City Council provided direction to staff but there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation to Former Mayor Ury

  Mayor MacLean presented Council Member Ury with a gavel plaque in recognition of
  his service as Mayor in 2009.

P2.  Opening Remarks by Mayor MacLean

  The City Council received remarks from Mayor MacLean.

P3.  Plaque of Appreciation to the City of Mission Viejo for Support of the Marines &
  Sailors of the Headquarters Battalion of the First Marine Division at Camp
  Pendleton

  Mayor MacLean received a plaque of appreciation from Colonel Michael S. Groen for
  the City’s support of the Marines and Sailors of the Headquarters Battalion of the First
  Marines Division, Camp Pendleton.

City Council Minutes  2  January 4, 2010
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Will Kempton, Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA): Mr. Kempton formally
introduced himself as the new Chief Executive Officer of OCTA. He stated that he hopes to
provide leadership and stability as the new CEO and he looks forward to working with City as
they continue efforts to improve mobility across the County.

Neil Lonsinger, M.V.: inquired about agenda item 10 and he asked why the audit cannot be done
in-house. He further questioned last year’s City Council stipend increase and he stated that those
who collect Social Security are not getting an increase this year.

Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: stated that the City’s elected officials act very immaturely and he
expressed concern about the Council handling taxpayers’ money by spending unnecessary funds
on unnecessary projects.

Sharon Cody, M.V.: stated that the City should sue the individuals responsible for the $270,000
recall election.

Susan Sellers, M.V.: echoed the prior comments and requested that the City sue residents Dale
Tyler and Connie Lee to recoup the money being spent on an election that she feels is fraudulent.

Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: announced that the Marine Adoption Committee needs evening wear
(gowns and accessories) and those donated will be stored for the ball in October. She also
announced that seasonal flu and H1N1 vaccines will be available on Tuesday, January 5 in Lake
Forest between 9:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. and on Wednesday, January 6 at the Murray Community
Center in Mission Viejo from 10:00. a.m. to 2:00 p.m.

Paulina Finorio, M.V.: complained about peculiar activities occurring in her neighborhood and
around the City.

Helen Workun, M.V.: urged residents to vote no on the recall of Lance MacLean in order to
preserve the quality of life and to enjoy what we have in our beautiful City.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 9 and 10 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  3  January 4, 2010
 1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular Meeting of December 7, 2009, as presented.

3.  Check Register dated November 20, 2009, in the amount of $1,386,777.92

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated November 27, 2009, in the amount of $1,601,137.20

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer's Monthly Report for October 2009

  Received and filed.

6.  Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for October 2009

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer's Monthly Report for October 2009

  Received and filed.

8.  Mileage Reimbursement

  Approved Resolution No. 10-01 Adopting the 2010 Standard IRS Mileage
  Reimbursement Rate of 50.0 Cents Per Mile Effective January 1, 2010.

11.  Medical Center Road Pavement Resurfacing (CIP 838)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being

City Council Minutes  4  January 4, 2010
   filed with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

12.  Revised Orange County Taxi Administration Program (OCTAP) Regulations

  Adopted Resolution 10-02 Adopting Revised Orange County Taxi Administration
  Program Regulations.

13.  Investment of Proceeds of Mission Viejo Community Development Financing
  Authority Lease Revenue Refunding Bonds, 2009 Series A

  Adopted MVCDFA Resolution 10-01 Authorizing Investment of Bond Proceeds in the
  State Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF).

14.  Claim Against the City - Barrientos-Macias vs. The City of Mission Viejo

  Rejected claim.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

15.  Appeal of Planned Development Permit PDP2009-215 and Minor Exception
  ME2009-97 filed by Gil Gonzalez of Trillium Consulting, Inc., agent for AT&T
  Wireless of the Planning and Transportation Commission’s September 28, 2009
  denial of a petition submitted by Jason Kozora of Trillium Consulting, Inc., agent
  for AT&T Mobility, to construct a wireless telecommunication facility at an existing
  True Value Hardware Store, Mission Viejo MarketPlace shopping center, 26006
  Marguerite Parkway, in the CC (Commercial Community) zone (Continued from
  the meeting of December 7, 2009)

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Tim Martin, Associate Planner, presented a visual representation of the proposed cell
  tower via architectural drawings/elevations and photographs from neighbors' back yards.

  Mayor MacLean opened the public hearing at 6:55 p.m.

  Gil Gonzalez, Trillium Consulting, Inc., agent for AT&T Wireless: outlined the proposed
  wireless telecommunication facility and introduced new design options.

  The following spoke in opposition to the proposed wireless telecommunication facility:
  Ramnik Singh, M.V. and Doug George, M.V.

  Resident Mike Shivayi presented a petition containing the signatures of fifteen
  residents/neighbors who request denial of the AT&T proposal.

City Council Minutes  5  January 4, 2010
   The following presented written comments in opposition to the proposed antenna
  structure: Farzaneh Khamee, M.V. and Stefanie Shepanski, M.V.

  Gil Gonzalez, Trillium Consulting, Inc., agent for AT&T Wireless: provided a rebuttal
  and closing comments.

  Mayor MacLean closed the public hearing at 7:18 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to send this
  matter back to the Planning and Transportation Commission to allow the Commission to
  address the changes that were proposed by the appellant tonight and to allow the residents
  to provide input.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  By consensus, the City Council directed staff to require AT&T to fund the mailing of
  notices to residents so they will be aware that the matter is going back to the Planning
  and Transportation Commission.

OLD BUSINESS

16.  Appointment to Fill One Unscheduled Vacancy on the Planning and Transportation
  Commission (Continued from the meeting of December 7, 2009)

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  appoint Andre Hadzi-Pavlovic to the Planning and Transportation Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

17.  City Council Committee Representative Appointments

  Gail Reavis, M.V.: requested that the Mayor re-appoint her to serve on the Orange
  County Vector Control Board.

City Council Minutes  6  January 4, 2010
   Mayor MacLean appointed representatives to the committees/regional boards as follows:

  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency
  Representative – Council Member Ury
  Alternate – Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency
  Representative - Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Alternate – Mayor MacLean

  Measure M Growth Management Area 9 and 10 Interjurisdictional Forum
  Representative – Council Member Ledesma
  Alternate – Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

  California Joint Powers Insurance Authority
  Representative – Council Member Schlicht
  Alternate – Irwin B. Bornstein (Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services)

  Orange County Fire Authority Board of Directors
  Representative – Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Alternate – Mayor MacLean

  Orange County Council of Governments (General Assembly)
  Representative – Council Member Schlicht
  Alternate – Council Member Ledesma

  Transportation Corridor System
  Representative – Mayor MacLean
  Alternate – Council Member Ledesma

  League of California Cities and Orange County Division of the League of California
  Cities
  Representative – Mayor MacLean
  Alternate – Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

  South Orange County Major Investment Study (SOCMIS) Policy Working Group
  Representative – Council Member Ury
  Alternate – Mayor MacLean

City Council Minutes  7  January 4, 2010
   Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG)
  Representative – Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  (this Board does not allow for alternates)

  Orange County Vector Control District
  Representative – Council Member Ledesma
  (this Board does not allow for alternates)

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

9.  Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for the Alicia Parkway Traffic Light
  Synchronization Program Project

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about the synchronization project completion date and
  she asked if there was any progress on the concept of unrestricted left hand turns.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon replied that the latest schedule from OCTA
  indicates that timing and synchronization studies are expected to be complete during the
  first 6 months of this year with a monitoring and adjustment period to follow for the
  second 6 months. Regarding unprotected left turns, staff will request OCTA’s consultant
  to evaluate these as part of their studies.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor MacLean, to approve
  Amendment No. 1 to Memorandum of Understanding C-8-1403 with the Orange County
  Transportation Authority for the Alicia Parkway Traffic Light Synchronization Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

10.  Utility Bill Audit

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley asked for a staff report to provide clarification for residents who
  may have questions on the proposed audit.

  Joe Holtzman, M.V.: applauded the City for calling for this audit.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve
  the contract with Utility Cost Management LLC to perform a utility bill audit on a
  contingent fee basis.

City Council Minutes  8  January 4, 2010
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

18.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

19.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor MacLean announced that the Foothill/Eastern TCA did not meet over the
  holidays.

20.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma announced that the San Joaquin Hills TCA did not meet over
  the holidays.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

21.  Support for AB 1590 to Stop the Sale of State-Owned Property That is Home to the
  Orange County Fair and Event Center

  Deputy City Manager Karen Wylie presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to
  direct staff to send a letter in support of AB 1590 to the Governor and the Bill's author.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Attorney’s Report

22.  Elections Code: Voter Information Regarding Recall Election Voting Process

City Council Minutes  9  January 4, 2010
   City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in opposition to the distribution of the voter information material:
  Larry Gilbert, M.V.; Mark Dobrilovic, M.V.; Gail Reavis, M.V.; Linda Barnes, M.V.;
  and Rick Sandzimier, M.V.

  The following presented a written statement in favor of distribution of the voter education
  material: Sharon Cody, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to
  authorize staff to release the educational material via the City’s web site and the
  eNewsletter.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

23.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht read a quote from Martin Luther King, Jr. concluding that one must
take a position because it is right.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury stated that it will be a very interesting month and he hopes that cool heads
will prevail. He wished everyone a happy New Year and he stated that it will be an outstanding
year and he looks forward to the challenges ahead.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Po Tem Kelley publicly apologized, on behalf of the City Council, for the treatment that
two of the public speakers had to endure this evening. She stated that she is especially unhappy
that Commissioner Sandzimier was vilified yet the person who was disruptive and had to be

City Council Minutes  10  January 4, 2010
 removed from the Council Chamber was one of Council Member Schlicht’s Commissioners.
She expressed hope that the behavior that we are seeing at these Council Meetings will change.
Mayor Pro Tem Kelley recounted the wonderful holiday season she spent with her family and
she expressed her thanks to the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for Santa’s Workshop.
They provided hours and hours of enjoyment for the children of our community and she offered
special thanks to the Chairman of Santa’s Workshop, Don Asay, the President of the Activities
Committee, Del Holt, as well as the many committee members who bring this special event to
our City. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley congratulated Mission Viejo Police Services’ 2009 Employee
of the Year, Deputy Jay Christian and Fire Captain Jack Perisho, Mission Viejo’s top Fire
Authority Employee of the Year. She stated that we are grateful for the excellence of their
service. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley reminded residents that there will be a flu shot clinic in Lake
Forest on Tuesday, January 5 and another clinic in Mission Viejo on January 6, at the Murray
Community Center for both seasonal and H1N1 vaccines. She also announced that she is
organizing another blood drive in honor of our Hometown Hero, Lance Corporal Alex Minsky.
She encouraged residents to mark their calendars and donate blood on January 12, 2010, from
10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. in the Saddleback Room at City Hall. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley offered
special thanks to an unsung hero, Barbara Brazil, who singlehandedly obtained forty seven ball
gowns for the wives of the young marines attending the birthday ball. Lastly, she announced that
the Community of Character word for the month of January is perseverance and she wished
everyone a happy New Year.

Council Member Schlicht vacated the dais at 8:49 p.m. and returned at 8:51 p.m.

Mayor MacLean

Mayor MacLean stated that the Council tries to emulate the Community of Character qualities
and set an example for the community. He apologized to audience-members who had to witness
outbursts from the audience and at the dais this evening. He reminded his colleagues that he
opened the meeting suggesting a civil dialogue but he failed to convince some. Mayor MacLean
stated that recalls are intended to remove someone who is accused of malfeasance and that they
were never intended to remove someone because of a disagreement on policy issues.

Council Member Schlicht departed the meeting at 8:55 p.m. and did not return.

Mayor MacLean drew attention to the fact that Council Member Schlicht just left the dais in
protest to his comments. He noted that with hindsight, everyone can look back and say they
would have done some things differently but by and large he stands behind every vote that he has
made. Mayor MacLean stated that his biggest frustration is the way that the recall was presented
to residents by taking a small element of truth and turning it into a lie. He cited the Casta del Sol
golf course proposal and stated that the Council did their job of listening to the developer,
directing them to hold public meetings, and in the end, expressing that they were not interested in
the proposal. The Council also passed a unanimous moratorium to finalize that message. Mayor
MacLean stated that the recall proponents are willing to lie and sell their souls because they
disagree with the policy direction of the City. He reminded his colleagues that a recent survey
showed that 99% of the residents are happy with the way things are going in Mission Viejo, even

City Council Minutes  11  January 4, 2010
 during this difficult economy. While other cities are worrying about crime rates, tremendous
gridlock, potholes, and bankruptcy, our residents complain about dying plants, rocks that were
removed from a corner, or the rose parade float. He stated that those individuals who are
screaming that the Council is spending the City into oblivion are flat out lying. He stated that he
has consistently voted to improve and maintain roads and private property rights and to allege
that he singlehandedly approved projects is false. Council Members do not vote individually to
move things forward; it takes at least three votes. Mayor MacLean stated that dollars spent for
the recall election could be used for a community benefit, not to serve the purposes of a small
group that want to take over power and shut down the quality of life. He noted that the Council,
as representatives, are elected to provide programs and services to the residents and to assure an
adequate amount of reserves and there seems to be a fundamental misunderstanding of how
government operates. Mayor MacLean stated that he stands by all of his votes, he has no regrets,
and he thanked his colleagues for selecting him as Mayor this year.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:04 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor MacLean adjourned the meeting to Monday, January 18, 2010, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of January 18, 2010

City Council Minutes  12  January 4, 2010
